name: Ajwain (Carom Seeds)
uses: A common kitchen remedy for gas, stomach pain, indigestion and bloating. Also used for coughs and blocked nose.
how_to_take: Chew half a teaspoon of seeds with warm water, or boil a teaspoon of seeds in a glass of water and sip it warm.
caution: Too much can cause heartburn. Avoid large amounts in pregnancy.

name: Cumin (Jeera)
uses: Used after meals to ease indigestion, gas, bloating and mild stomach pain.
how_to_take: Boil a teaspoon of seeds in a glass of water for a few minutes and sip it warm (jeera water).
caution: Large amounts may cause heartburn and can lower blood sugar a little. Use only food amounts in pregnancy.

name: Fennel (Saunf)
uses: Used for gas, bloating, cramps and as a mouth freshener after meals.
how_to_take: Chew half a teaspoon of seeds after meals, or steep a teaspoon in hot water for 10 minutes as tea.
caution: Avoid medicinal amounts in pregnancy. People allergic to carrot or celery may react. Do not give fennel oil to children.

name: Clove (Laung)
uses: Traditionally used for toothache, sore throat and cough because of its numbing, antiseptic effect.
how_to_take: Hold one whole clove gently near the sore tooth for a short time, or add one or two to hot tea for a sore throat.
caution: Clove oil must be diluted and can burn gums. Large amounts can thin blood. Not for young children.

name: Black Pepper (Kali Mirch)
uses: A warming spice used in kadha and tea for colds, cough and sore throat, and to help digestion.
how_to_take: A pinch of powder in warm tea or kadha with tulsi and ginger, or with a little honey.
caution: Can irritate the stomach, especially with ulcers or acid reflux. It can change how some medicines are absorbed.

name: Triphala
scientific: Terminalia chebula, T. bellirica, Phyllanthus emblica
uses: A classic three-fruit blend used to ease constipation and support digestion.
how_to_take: Half a teaspoon of powder in warm water at bedtime.
caution: Can cause loose stools. Avoid in pregnancy and during diarrhea. May interact with blood thinners and diabetes medicines.

name: Isabgol (Psyllium Husk)
uses: A fiber that softens stool for constipation and can also firm up loose stools.
how_to_take: One teaspoon in a full glass of water, drunk right away, followed by another glass of water.
caution: Always take with plenty of water, or it can cause choking or blockage. Take it 2 hours apart from other medicines.

name: Bael (Wood Apple)
uses: Traditionally used for loose motions and digestive upset.
how_to_take: Ripe fruit pulp as a drink (sherbet), or a teaspoon of dried bael powder in water.
caution: May lower blood sugar. Too much can cause constipation. With diarrhea, also drink plenty of fluids and ORS.

name: Coriander Seeds (Dhania)
uses: Used to cool the body, ease indigestion and acidity, and soothe a burning feeling while passing urine.
how_to_take: Soak a teaspoon of seeds in a glass of water overnight, strain and drink in the morning.
caution: May lower blood sugar and blood pressure a little. Rarely causes allergic reactions.

name: Curry Leaves
uses: Used in food and home remedies for hair health, nausea and digestion.
how_to_take: Chew 8 to 10 fresh leaves in the morning, or use them generously in cooking.
caution: Safe in food amounts. Large medicinal amounts may add to the effect of diabetes medicines.

name: Lemongrass
uses: A fragrant tea herb used for colds, mild fever, stomach cramps and stress.
how_to_take: Simmer a crushed fresh stalk in water for 5 to 10 minutes and sip as tea.
caution: Avoid medicinal amounts in pregnancy. May cause dizziness or low blood pressure in some people.

name: Eucalyptus
uses: Steam inhalation is traditionally used to open a blocked nose and ease chest congestion.
how_to_take: Add a few leaves (or 2 to 3 drops of oil) to a bowl of hot water and breathe the steam for a few minutes, with a towel over your head and eyes closed.
caution: Never swallow the oil. Keep away from the faces of young children. Be careful not to scald yourself. Can trigger asthma in some people.

name: Shatavari
uses: Traditionally used as a women's health tonic for periods, lactation and menopause symptoms.
how_to_take: Half a teaspoon of powder in warm milk, once a day.
caution: Ask a doctor first if pregnant, or if you have a hormone-sensitive condition. Can cause swelling or allergy in some people.

name: Bitter Gourd (Karela)
uses: Used in food and as juice to support healthy blood sugar.
how_to_take: Cooked as a vegetable, or a small glass of fresh juice (diluted) in the morning.
caution: Can drop blood sugar too far with diabetes medicines. Avoid in pregnancy. May upset the stomach.

name: Jamun (Java Plum)
uses: The fruit and dried seed powder are traditionally used to support blood sugar and settle loose motions.
how_to_take: A handful of fruit in season, or half a teaspoon of seed powder in water.
caution: Lowers blood sugar, so take care with diabetes medicines and before surgery.
